items.title: SSH private key
items.why: Logs in to every server and pushes to every Git host that trusts the key. Without a passphrase, the file alone is enough.

items.title: SSH public key
items.why: Public. Read to name the private key next to it by its type and fingerprint.

items.title: AWS credentials file
items.why: Static access keys work from anywhere until someone rotates them.

items.title: AWS config
items.why: Can hold access keys too, and names the roles and SSO sessions every profile can use.

items.title: AWS cached session tokens
items.why: Short-lived, but valid for hours: enough to copy everything a role can read.

items.title: Google Cloud CLI credentials
items.why: Refresh tokens for every account gcloud is signed in to; they do not expire on their own.

items.title: Google application default credentials
items.why: Every Google client library on the machine uses this file: a refresh token or a service account key.

items.title: Azure CLI tokens and service principal secrets
items.why: Signed-in sessions, and on Linux service principal secrets in plain JSON.

items.title: GitHub CLI login
items.why: A GitHub token with the scopes you granted gh: push, create repositories, read private code. In the keyring, `gh auth token` still prints it to anyone running as you.

items.title: Git credential store
items.why: Plain-text passwords and tokens for every Git host listed in it.

items.title: netrc passwords
items.why: Plain-text logins that curl, git and package managers use without asking.

items.title: npm token
items.why: Publishes packages under your name: a supply-chain attack waiting for one command.

items.title: PyPI token
items.why: Publishes packages under your name.

items.title: Cargo registry token
items.why: Publishes crates under your name.

items.title: Docker registry logins
items.why: Without a credential store, registry passwords sit in config.json, base64-encoded: push images as you.

items.title: Kubernetes config
items.why: Cluster access with your rights, often cluster-admin on development clusters.

items.title: Hugging Face token
items.why: Reads private models and datasets, and with write scope pushes to them.

items.title: Supabase access token
items.why: Manages every Supabase project of the account: databases, keys, functions.

items.title: Terraform Cloud token
items.why: Runs plans and applies, and reads state, which often holds more secrets.

items.title: Vault token
items.why: Reads every secret its policies allow, from the place you keep secrets.

items.title: pass password store
items.why: Encrypted with gpg; while gpg-agent holds the key, any process running as you can decrypt it.

items.title: 1Password CLI
items.why: With the app integration, `op` reads items as long as the app is unlocked.

items.title: Browser session cookies
items.why: A copied cookie database signs in to every site you are signed in to, without a password or a second factor.

items.title: Coding agent login token
items.why: The agent's own account: an injected agent can send the token away and keep using your subscription or API key.

items.title: Coding agent transcripts and history
items.why: Plain text that keeps whatever tools printed, including secrets read in earlier sessions.

items.title: .env file
items.why: Application secrets for the project at hand: database passwords, API keys, signing secrets.

items.title: Secret-looking environment variables
items.why: Inherited by every process the agent starts; one `env` command prints them all.

items.title: ssh-agent socket
items.why: Signs with every loaded key: log in and push as you without ever reading a key file.

items.title: Docker socket
items.why: Whoever can write to it can start a container that mounts the whole disk: root on the machine.

items.title: gpg-agent socket
items.why: Decrypts and signs for any client while a passphrase is cached.

items.title: Coding agent configuration
items.why: Read as data, never run: it decides what the agent may do. Not a secret by itself, though values such as MCP environment variables are dropped while parsing.

items.title: Sandbox programs
items.why: Whether an agent's OS sandbox can run here is decided by whether its program exists; it is never run.
